question: Is there room to write MT content without disturbing QA content? Concretely: (1) does the QA routing Gram C0 = E_q[a(q)a(q)^T] at top_t=512 have an approximate null space at all, and (2) does MT routing energy actually live in it? These two jointly decide whether the null-space / projection family (LIT-011 AlphaEdit, LIT-012 Adam-NSCL/OWM/GPM, LIT-017 null-space key placement) is viable here.
variable_under_test: none (forward-pass-only geometry measurement on the untouched Phase-1 cartridge; QA eval split vs MT eval split)
baseline_ref: ORACLE-WRITE (same Phase-1 cache, same eval-time softmax convention, same tf-idf top-32 slot union)

numbers.note: No training and no eval was run. This task is forward passes only, so no CE loss is reported (WORKERS.md: never fabricate a number).

definition.routing_vector: a(q) = softmax(q K_cart^T / sqrt(d)) over the 512 cartridge slots — exactly the design matrix X at cartridges/am/value_solve.py:86 with top_t=512. Recovered as w[:, :512] / w[:, :512].sum() from the FULL eval-time softmax over [512 slots || own-sequence causal prefix], because a softmax restricted to a subset is the renormalised subset softmax. Same forward/hook path as ORACLE-WRITE/measure_route_mass.py.
definition.gram: C = (1/N) sum_q a(q) a(q)^T per (layer, KV-head); N = all query positions x all query heads of that KV group.
definition.rho: rho(r) = tr(P_r C_MT)/tr(C_MT) with P_r = I - U_r U_r^T, U_r = top-r eigenvectors of the QA Gram C0. rho_QA(r) is the identical statistic on C0 itself and is the in-sample leakage control.
definition.aggregation: All headline numbers are means over the 288 (layer, KV-head) pairs unless labelled 'pooled' (= metrics of the Gram averaged over all 288 heads).

Q1_qa_gram_spectrum_top_t_512.verdict: The projector P is emphatically NOT zero at top_t=512: the spectrum is dominated by a single direction (83% of energy on average, 91% pooled) and 439 of 512 dimensions carry under 1% of QA routing energy.

Q2_rho_mt_energy_in_qa_nullspace.verdict: MT routing energy does NOT live in QA's null space. At the GPM 99%-energy rule rho_MT = 0.012, i.e. 98.8% of MT's routing energy sits inside the 73-dimensional subspace QA occupies, and the in-sample QA floor at the same rank is 0.0166 at r=73 / 0.0096 at the rule — MT exceeds QA's own tail by only 13-65%.

cross_check_vs_ORACLE_WRITE.note: [ORACLE-WRITE reported, DIAG-ROUTING independently recomputed] — agreement to 4-6 significant figures confirms the measurement convention is identical.

Q4_qa_mt_mean_routing_overlap.verdict: The two tasks want the same slots. LIT-013 predicted histogram intersection > 0.5 and named < 0.2 as the falsifier for the whole interference family; we measure 0.963.

diagnostics.raw_arrays: research_loop/state/diagnostics/DIAG-ROUTING.json (per-layer arrays for all four quantities + provenance) and DIAG-ROUTING.npz (per-(layer,head) QA eigenvalues, MT energy per QA eigendirection, both mean routing vectors, all rank and rho arrays).

wandb_note: Per-layer series are logged as diag/<group>/<key> with step=layer; the mean-over-288-heads scalars are in the run summary under diagmean/* and the pooled-Gram scalars under pooled/*. (The first summary write used bare diag/* names that collided with the per-layer log keys; the diagmean/* and pooled/* keys were written afterwards via the wandb API and are the authoritative scalars.)
command: bash research_loop/results/DIAG-ROUTING/launch_diag_routing.sh  (backgrounded; claims one GPU by flock, exports PYTHONPATH=/tmp/amsnap_diagrouting, then runs research_loop/results/DIAG-ROUTING/measure_routing_geometry.py with PHASE1_CACHE=outputs/phase1_selfdistill_qwen512/cache_last.pt, EVAL_SPECS='QA:data/qasper/eval/qasper_eval_QA.parquet,MT:data/qasper/eval/qasper_eval_MT.parquet', SLOTS_RUN_DIR=<ORACLE-WRITE control run dir, for the top-32 union>, WANDB_DISABLED=0, RUN_NAME=DIAG-ROUTING_geometry, WANDB_GROUP=B-ROUTE). NO source file under cartridges/ was edited; two new standalone files were created under research_loop/results/DIAG-ROUTING/.
observations: The QA routing Gram at top_t=512 is drastically low-rank: averaged over the 288 (layer, KV-head) pairs the top eigenvector carries 83% of QA routing energy (91% pooled), the participation effective rank is 1.97, and 439 of 512 dimensions together hold under 1% of the energy — so an approximate null space at large support unambiguously exists and AlphaEdit's projector P is far from zero there (LIT-011's structural caveat is answered: the family is not vacuous at top_t=512, only at small t). MT routing energy nevertheless does not live in that null space: rho_MT = 0.0120 at GPM's 99%-energy rule, 0.0423 if the top 32 QA directions are forbidden, and 0.00945 at rank 128, against an in-sample QA leakage floor of 0.0096 / 0.0361 / 0.00708 at the same ranks — i.e. MT's out-of-subspace energy exceeds QA's own tail by only 13-65%, and no layer reaches rho_MT above 0.0147 at the 99% rule (per-head maximum 0.209 at rank 73). The two tasks want the same slots: the mean routing vectors have cosine 0.99899 (minimum 0.9755 over 288 heads), histogram intersection 0.963, and top-32 slot-set overlap 0.914 — LIT-013 named histogram intersection < 0.2 as the falsifier for the whole interference family and we measure the opposite extreme. mass_on_S at top_t=512 is the whole cartridge mass, 0.5697 for QA queries and 0.5879 for MT queries (ratio 1.032), versus 0.0827 / 0.0896 on the tf-idf top-32 union (ratio 1.083), so moving to full support raises the write's attention bandwidth 6.6x; routing is extremely spiky in both cases, 1.946 nats for QA and 2.009 for MT, i.e. an effective 14.4 vs 15.1 of 512 slots, with MT no more diffuse than QA. The tf-idf-union and total-cartridge masses reproduce ORACLE-WRITE's Phase-1 numbers to 4-6 significant figures (0.08961 vs 0.08956, 0.08272 vs 0.08272, 0.58787 vs 0.58787, 0.56967 vs 0.56967) from an independent implementation, so the convention is confirmed comparable. What this rules out: an MT-specific routing subspace does not exist at any threshold we tested, so null-space value projection (LIT-011/012) cannot buy acquisition here — writing inside QA's approximate null space discards ~99% of MT's routing leverage — and it can only act as a retention operator, which is what the board already suspected but had no number for; the near-total slot overlap likewise leaves a discrete 'pick slots QA is blind to' selector (LIT-013 mass_margin, LIT-017's discrete variant) at most ~9% of slots to work with among the existing 512 cartridge keys. Caveats: rho_QA is by construction in-sample (it is one minus the cumulative eigenvalue fraction of the very Gram it is measured against), so a held-out QA control would raise the floor and shrink the MT/QA contrast further, not widen it; the measurement is of routing vectors on the frozen Phase-1 keys and says nothing directly about LIT-017's 128-dimensional query second moment Q0, which would need synthetic keys that do not yet exist; and everything here is on the untouched Phase-1 cartridge, not on a post-write cache.
